title: Mechanica
angle: No tech words: a real mechanic, a real page. The spine — get this one muscle-memory and eight of the nine are 80% rehearsed.
endline: Don't trust the AI. Trust the manual.

marks.do: Type mt-07 → 2018 → ✓. Leave the ingest running.
His two reasons: 95%, and $4 a question.
CHAT → chain is loose, what do I do.
Mic → how much engine oil does it take.
Back — the MT-07 is ready. Type oil.

slides.title: Mechanica
slides.line: Don't trust the AI. Trust the manual.
slides.meta: We just get you to the page
notes: *Don't rush it.* Say the title, then stop talking for two seconds. The whole pitch is a reversal — an AI that refuses to answer — and reversals need a beat.
Alternative art if you want the product on screen from second one: ~general/01-landing.png~.
Throughout: no model names, no vendor names, no architecture. If someone wants that they will ask, and the answer lives in Q&A.

slides.text: He fixes bikes for a living. About a fifth of his working week he is not fixing bikes — he is looking for a page.
slides.sub: *400 hours a year.* At a German shop rate that is *EUR 36–48k* of work he could have billed.
notes: *Name him, don't dramatise him.* "A friend of mine." Not "a customer", not "shops everywhere". One person is more convincing than a market, and the room knows the difference.
Say ~he says~ out loud. The 20% is his estimate; the 400 hours and the euros are arithmetic on his number and an assumed 2,000-hour year. Say ~that's arithmetic on his number~.
While this is on screen the MT-07 2018 ingest you started at 0:20 is running in the background. Do not look at it.

defs.d: share of his working time spent looking for a page — HIS estimate, reported by the founder (assumed). Always say "he says".
20% × 2,000 h — arithmetic on his number and an assumed 2,000-hour year (computed).
400 h × EUR 90–120/h (computed). ramp/numbers.md defends EUR 24,640 after recovery and utilisation.

items.label: right — and he signs for the 5%
items.sub: "95% right isn't enough when I sign for the 5%."

items.label: a question, when he tried it
items.sub: The model had to read a 500-page manual. He hit his limit by lunchtime.

notes: *Let the two numbers sit alone.* No bullets. 95% and $4. Say them as ~his~ reasons, not your argument.
You are not attacking AI — you are agreeing with a skeptic, which buys you everything you do next.
His ~$4 is *his* bill on *his* manual. Our own measured naive worst case is $12.40 and our median is $1.37. Three different numbers — never blend them.

defs.d: his line, quoted: "95% right isn't enough when I sign for the 5%." His number, not ours.
what one question cost him when he tried an LLM — HIS bill (assumed). Not the same measurement as our $12.40.

notes: "So we built the opposite of a chatbot. Mechanica never answers. It finds the page in the manufacturer's own manual and puts your finger on the line."

This slide is optional — it is the *user path* diagram from general.md, redrawn. If you are running short, cut it and narrate the path over the demo instead. Never cut the page at 2:20 or the chat at 3:15.
Do not say the word architecture. Three steps: bike, question, pages.

slides.title: Start with the bike
slides.line: *27,751 vehicles* — motorcycles and cars. Type it, photograph it, or scan the VIN.
points: 13,537 of them already carry a free official manual
VIN → the exact bike in 1.3 s
notes: *Narrate the taps, not the screen.* "Type it. Tap it." They should feel how few taps there are.
Say the words "or photograph it, or scan the VIN" and move on. Don't explain either path unless asked.
Do not say ~17,556 manuals~ or "seventeen thousand". Never call 13,537 manuals — it is vehicles carrying a free manual.

slides.title: The exact one
slides.line: Year and market, because a torque figure from the wrong year is how you strip a thread.
points: A 2024 and a 2021 are different machines.
They care about the boring part — that is the point.
notes: Tap the KTM 390 DUKE card, then 2024. Two taps, no explanation.
This is the slide where a mechanic decides whether you have ever met one. The year gate is the tell.

slides.title: Say what's wrong
slides.line: Plain words in. The manual's own headings out — and the part lit on the bike.
points: `chain is loose` → *12.12 Checking the chain tension* p. 77–78
Those aren't our words. That is KTM's own table of contents.
notes: *The line that lands is "those aren't our words."* Point at the headings. 12.12 and 12.13 are KTM's own section numbers; that they look like a filing system is the point.
It didn't write anything. That is what they should feel.
If the 3D bike doesn't load it never blocks anything — carry on, the headings and the page are the point.

slides.title: The answer is a page
slides.line: KTM's page 77, marked on the two lines that answer — and *only* where we found that ink.
points: "If we can't find the ink, we don't draw the marker."
slides.caption: 143 printed pages, a hand-curated 20-section index. Tap ALL and the whole book is there.
notes: *This is the slide. Stop.* Let them read the marked line.

Then one sentence: "and the marker is only there because we found that text in KTM's PDF. If we can't find it, we don't draw it." That sentence is the entire trust story; everything else is convenience.
Right section first on *100% of the 130 in-scope* eval questions, and *0 of 20* off-topic questions answered instead of refused. Say it only if asked.

defs.d: printed pages in the demo manual, KTM 390 Duke 2024 (ktm-390-duke-2024-om-en).
right section first, in-scope questions — 100% of 130, api/eval/report.md (measured).
off-topic questions returned empty instead of guessed at — the oos category, 100% empty (measured).

And that the quotes are cut out of the page by *our server*, not written by the model. Verbatim by construction, not by trust.
Tap a [p. 78] chip live — the page appears. Even the chatty part is leashed.

slides.title: general.md — check this list the morning of

groups.label: This pitch
items: Do not say 17,556 manuals, or "seventeen thousand".
Do not promise full offline. The app, the vehicle list, the chapters and the pages you already opened work with the network off; fetching a new manual, chat and voice do not.
Do not say "none of our service manuals are free" — 182 service rows, 15 of them paid, subscription or dealer-login only.

groups.label: All nine, global
items: ElevenLabs voice is never "live" — say "built, one key away". The live voice is Deepgram, and deepgram: true.
The 3D backdrop is a technical grid. No panorama, no photographic workshop scene — there is none.
Dropbox folder sync and Climate Fit are "built, deploying", not deployed.
Never quote a running ledger total without the date beside it. Prefer not quoting it.
Never call 13,537 "manuals" — it is vehicles carrying a free manual. Distinct fetchable PDFs is 14,770.
Never call 4,081 and 1,489 the same number: owner-typed over every row vs the free-English subset.
There is no checkout. "Live prices", never "buy".
